title: Batteries
steps: Collect all types of used batteries (AA, AAA, button cells, rechargeable, etc.) from home and keep them separate from other household waste.
Place batteries in a sealed, non-metal container (like a plastic box) to prevent short circuits. Store away from children, pets, and heat sources.

Check local guidelines: some areas require different types of batteries (alkaline, lithium, rechargeable) to be collected separately. Verify instructions from your local recycling center or municipality.
Locate a recycling center using online tools, apps, or your municipality website. Some supermarkets and electronic stores have designated battery collection bins.
Carry your stored batteries carefully to avoid damage or leaks. Keep the container upright and secure during transport.
At the recycling center, hand over the batteries to staff or place them in the designated battery recycling bin. Ensure the center accepts your battery types.
Verify acceptance if unsure and encourage friends and family to recycle batteries properly.
precautions: Never throw batteries in regular trash.
Do not burn or puncture batteries, as they can leak toxic chemicals or explode.
Keep batteries away from water or high heat.
Separate different types of batteries when required by local guidelines.
Store batteries safely before transport to avoid leaks or short circuits.
